$comment: Editable narrative layer for the project dashboard. Numbers come live from GitHub at generation time (npm run dashboard); this file holds the story, decisions, and curation that no API can produce. Keep entries short — one line each. New ideas: add to ideas[] here, and promote to a GitHub issue when they become real work so they enter the metrics.
product_summary: VoxTable answers a restaurant's phone with a voice AI (Bella), takes the booking or pickup order, writes it to the database, and shows it live on the dashboard and kitchen display. Built by BitePerk Pty Ltd. First venue live: Natalia's Bistro (Sydney). Second install: Cuban Corner (staging).
where_we_are: Staging runs end-to-end on Cloud Run with its own Twilio number and Retell workspace, and every merge to integration deploys there automatically once CI passes. Production still runs on the original VM and is deployed by hand — moving it onto Cloud Run is the cutover that go-live planning revolves around. The board's Production Go Live milestone (23 Aug) tracks exactly what stands between here and there.

executive_summary_curated.win: Staging is a real environment now — own phone number, own Retell workspace, auto-deployed on every merge, rehearsable end to end.
executive_summary_curated.risk: Telephony compliance is the long pole: sender-ID registration binds to one Twilio account, and the account-architecture decision (#166) gates it.
executive_summary_curated.decision_needed: Settle the Twilio ISV/subaccount model (#166) before any venue is auto-provisioned — it cannot be rehearsed in staging and is expensive to redo.

decisions.title: integration-first branching
decisions.rationale: Work merges to integration (auto-deploys staging); main is release-only, reached by promotion. Merged no longer means live.

decisions.title: Staging boots from the database, not env vars
decisions.rationale: Per-restaurant identifiers are data. Closed platform PR #20, shipped as #107 — staging needs no per-venue config to boot.

decisions.title: No extra rollback tooling
decisions.rationale: Deploy recovery is a manual Cloud Run revision rollback; production deploys come from main only (review on #100).

decisions.title: Cloud SQL native backups
decisions.rationale: Postgres backup is GCP-native (automated backups + PITR), not a repo-side upload chain (review on #103).

decisions.title: Prove it in staging, then repeat it in production
decisions.rationale: Promotion means five different things (code, image, infra, schema, vendor config) and only code is automatic — the doctrine is written into CLAUDE.md with the honest list of what staging cannot rehearse.

decisions.title: main is protected
decisions.rationale: PR + green CI required, force-push blocked; the production GitHub environment only accepts deploys from main.

decisions.title: Fresh vendor estate under BitePerk
decisions.rationale: New Retell workspace and Twilio accounts under biteperk.com.au identities; the legacy Algorythmos accounts stay funded as rollback until cutover completes.

curated_risks.risk: Dependabot opened major-version bumps (vite 6→8, Tailwind 3→4) that could sit unreviewed and rot
Production image is rebuilt on main under a version tag — staging proved a different artifact (promotion-by-digest not yet done)
Legacy Algorythmos vendor accounts still carry pieces of production (recordings, rollback path) until the estate migration completes
